utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. The commander and then our command discussed what we should do next, because we had received approval from Sarajevo to withdraw -- or we hadn't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Nobody from Sarajevo contacted us.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So what were the competing arguments about staying or going?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we were expecting a message and we hadn't received any, this meant the orders we had were still valid and we were supposed to take part in the operation that was being conducted in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you told that you were required to stay on?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander told me that, that the operation was continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What else did your commander tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He just said that we should proceed and that I should prepare the men for the continuation of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: How long did you stay there in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was from the 8th or 9th until the 19th or 20th of September. I think it was about 12 days in all, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what did you do on the 19th of September?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that that was when the operation ended. And a request was made to the commander that we should stay there at the positions that we had taken, but my commander did not accept this, and we withdrew to Sarajevo with the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And once you got back to Sarajevo, did you then write this report that I've already showed you? And that is Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: -- 270, Your Honours. Can I have this report back on the screen, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, you've looked at this report. Can you tell me whether there is any mention of the murders in Grabovica in this report that you wrote after you came back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: There is no mention of the murders in this report because this is a report about the combat task. And I did not feel it appropriate, nor did my commander, because he signed the report, too -- he asked that I sign it as well, although I was not really competent to sign it. We didn't mention anything happening. I'm referring to these events, the murders and so on. This was purely a combat report on offensive operations during the military operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any investigations into this matter?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody ever called me until 1998, when I was summoned to the cantonal court in Sarajevo, and that was the first time I made a statement about the events in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And while you were in Grabovica on those particular dates - this is the 8th, 9th, and the 10th, up to 19th September - did you see anything being done about those murders?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything being done.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you or your commander report this once you got back to Sarajevo, other than this report that you've written? Did you tell anybody else about it?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't inform anyone because it wasn't within my competence. I don't know whether the commander did or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And in October 1993, did you change your position?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: In respect of your unit. Did you then replace Adnan Solakovic?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Okovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just start off by asking that the witness be provided with a copy of that report. Just give me a moment. Sorry, Mr. Okovic. It's, I think, P271. It might be MFI271 at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Okovic, the document that's going to be shown is that report dated the - 270 it might be - the report dated 25th of September, 1993, that you signed off on after your return from -- from Herzegovina. Do you have that report on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm really just concerned right now to try to get the dates as accurately as possible. And if it helps you to look at this document, feel free to. And if the document doesn't help, you'd better say so as well. But it's accurate that the -- the company set off late on the 7th of September -- the company of the 2nd Independent Battalion, I should say, set off late on the 7th of September and went through the tunnel sometime that night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at that time, you were in command of those units because Adnan Solakovic was going to come down the following day. Was that the plan at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you arrived at Jablanica the following morning at about 0815 hours, and you halted at the Zulfikar -- the Zulfikar base in Donja Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And at that time, did you personally meet with Zuka -- or, sorry, perhaps I should ask you this: Had you met Zulfikar Alispago personally before this time?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, during the events at Igman. I don't know exactly the date when Igman was falling. That was the first time that we met, during combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And would that be in late July -- I understand you don't remember the exact dates. Would that be in late July or perhaps early August of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so. I'm not sure about the dates, but it was during the fall of Igman and the cutting of the corridor to Gorazde. That's when my unit was also assigned to defend Igman and that was the first time that I met Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So when you arrived in Jablanica, Donja Jablanica, on the morning of the 8th of September, did you see -- did you recognise Zulfikar Alispago at his base and did you speak to him personally?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did he explain to you where your unit was to be based -- to be billeted, I should say?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: He gave me a logistics person, who showed me where we would be billeted. I didn't know where Grabovica was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand. Just thinking back the best way you can, was the person who he delegated to help you with the billeting of the troops a person who had the name Spaga?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that was his name. Spaga or Spago, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And just to be -- just to be very clear, because none of us were actually there: This person Spaga is different to Zuka. He's a person under the command of Zuka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, he was his logistics officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Okay. And to the best of your recollection, did this representative of Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago, then guide your three buses or your three trucks to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And to the best of your knowledge, you arrived in Grabovica sometime in the morning of the 8th of September; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And after that -- after arrival, did Zuka's representative there help to point out to you the appropriate houses that you could be billeted in?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that there were empty houses and that we can locate the command in a certain house. This is an old building from Austro-Hungarian times. That's where we set up the command. It was a former railway station. The rest of the unit were billeted in the two empty houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just to explain something that has been puzzling through the trial. There was in Grabovica at that time a railway line -- not an old railway line but a functioning railway line further up the hill at the back of the village. Do you recall the existence of that railway line?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that it existed, but up until that point in time, I had never gone up to the railway line. The railway line passes above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But when you refer to "the railway station," you're talking about a disused railway station that was down quite close to the river, as you pointed out on the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is an old railway, a narrow-track railway which was abolished, I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, upon arriving at that -- at that location, you've indicated that you found dwelling in that building a couple -- and I just want to be clear. Were there four people, four civilians in that building; namely, two refugees and also an elderly couple of Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a married couple in their 60s who lived there. They -- it was their house. They lived in that house. And two refugees from Stolac. That's what I found out from conversations with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just exercising your mind the best way you can now, do you recall whether one of those refugees was named or nicknamed Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, so far as you could see, relations between you and your soldiers, on the one hand, and these civilians, on the other hand, were correct and polite; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I think you've indicated that your unit was a multi-ethnic unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The truth is that you were fighting to save a multi-ethnic Bosnia protected by a multi-ethnic army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you were concerned, mistreatment of civilians, whatever their nationality was, was totally destructive to the war aims that you had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And quite apart from that policy sort of angle, you had friends from all different nationalities both in the unit and outside it; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when your units arrived in that village, the very last thing you expected was that some of those villagers would be brutally killed by any people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to ask you about the arrival of Vehbija Karic and Suljevic and Bilajac, who came to the village and spoke to you about the future conduct of the operation. When they arrived -- are you able to be -- you indicated that that took place around noon. I want to ask you how precise you're able to be about that time. Is it possible that it was later in the afternoon, or is it possible that it was earlier, or are you fairly confident that it was around noon?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was around noon. Actually, after 2.00 p.m. in the afternoon. I think that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were present -- had you ever dealt with Vehbija Karic before this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not really, since I was of lower rank. I wasn't an officer, so I didn't have contacts with senior officers. I had my own commander and communicated through him, even though I did know some of the people from this group from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, I understand that -- what you say about that. Do you recall whether Vehbija Karic arrived in the village in a car driven by his son? In other words, was Karic's son acting as the driver for those -- those officers?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who drove him. Somebody drove him, but I don't know whether that was his son or not. I'm hearing that for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Just to conclude that, did you meet the driver, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask that you be shown a map now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I wonder if the court staff could assist, please. This, I think, is -- it's the large map that we tendered. I think it's MFI135.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, that will be Defence Exhibit D131.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: D131. I'm sorry. Thank you. Yes, that is -- that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is a map with a heading on it of "Operation Neretva 93." You may have seen it before; you may not have. I'm going to ask you that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So I just wonder if that could be displayed, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Pardon me, Mr. Okovic. I apologise for that. Okay. Now, just first of all, do you recognise that as being a map of the Neretva Valley area in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'd just ask you to comment on a couple of aspects of it. Do you notice that it's signed at the top left in the -- with the name "Odobravam," "Komandant Rasim Delic"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And is that a form of writing that you're familiar with? In other words, that phrase "odobravam," meaning "I have approved it"?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you also see that in the capacity of Chief of Staff at the bottom right of that map there's another signature there, and that is the signature of Sefer Halilovic? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall being shown this map in the course of the -- of your trip to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: The first time I saw this map was during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How long ago was that? When you say "during the investigation," do you mean investigation for these proceedings here at The Hague or do you mean for some -- on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Fine. Okay. Very well. To your knowledge, at the time of this operation Sefer Halilovic had ceased to be the commander of the Bosnian army; is that correct? And in fact he was now Chief of Staff; whereas, Rasim Delic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood that situation at the time, I understood that up until that time, you only had the chief of the Main Staff and now the army was being formed and a commander of the army was being appointed, as well as a Chief of Staff. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I follow that. Did you come to know later on that Rasim Delic became the commander of the army altogether?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was immediately before this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And let me ask you: At the time of your involvement in this -- in this operation, did you know of Rasim Delic's appointment as head of the army, as the commander of the Main Staff? Or is that something you found out at a later time?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that shortly before leaving to go down there, I found out that a new commander had been appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Very well. So at the time when you were given your tasks in relation to the combat activities that you had to take -- oh, sorry. I'll withdraw that question. You ultimately took part in an operation called "Operation Defence of People's Rights." In fact, I'll just put the proper title to you, and if you'll excuse me a moment. You ultimately took part in an operation called "Defence of the People's Rights, Vrdi 93"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Would you -- it may be a bit -- a bit difficult at this length of time, but would you mind just looking on that map that's in front of you there and just seeing whether you can see depicted on that map an axis of attack that -- that is in the area where you ultimately did attack.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That would be that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Yes. Thanks. Very well. And I'm going to show you that order, the Vrdi 93 order in a moment, but I just want to keep things chronological at this stage, so -- very well, thank you. Now, coming back to that map that you've got there. Karic didn't show you that map? That's the short proposition.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And, in fact, part of the problem that you expressed to Karic was that you wanted to know about the HVO positions.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I was shown an empty map, a map that did not have the positions marked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And for that reason, it was resolved that you would go off with some other people the following morning to go and -- and go on a reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was it agreed at that stage with Karic, Bilajac, and Suljevic who you would go with, or was that dealt with later on?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Since we were supposed to be resubordinated to the command of Alispago Zulfikar and were supposed to operate along his axis and carry out the reconnaissance, which was subsequently agreed upon and approved that we go out and conduct this reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. All right. Now, you've indicated that at some stage on the afternoon or evening -- and I think your evidence was the evening, actually, so I'll withdraw that. You've indicated that on the evening of the 8th you went to a meeting of certain officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, in between the time of you meeting with Vehbija Karic, and Mr. Bilajac and Mr. Suljevic, did you notice anything going wrong in the village, such as gunshots being fired or civilians expressing fear or indeed any trouble of any sort in that first afternoon, or did things appear to be relatively peaceful while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing was happening. Everything was peaceful and normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As far as you could observe, the soldiers were behaving properly towards the local civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, that's what you expected -- no, well, I'll -- well, I mean, you expected your soldiers to behave properly towards civilians, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of the arrival during that time of any other troops? And in particular I'm referring to some units who came from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that units from Sarajevo were coming, and that's when I found out that the 9th and the 10th Mountain Brigade were coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And was it -- when you say you heard that, was it expressed to you by Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac that some other units were coming down from Sarajevo and were going to join in the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the three of them actually told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And -- but as to your own personal observations, did you see any elements of the 9th Brigade arrive in the village that afternoon while you were present?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What you can say is that while you were there, no soldiers behaved in a stupid, violent, or dangerous way, to your observation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you concede this possibility: That some of the 9th Brigade people might have arrived in that time but didn't behave in a way that drew attention to themselves so you didn't notice them? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's possible that I didn't see them, but as far as I know, I don't think that they had arrived at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time you set off to go to the meeting that you've described?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting in Konjic you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do mean that one.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It was already dusk. Actually, I think it was dark already. It was night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. So is it an accurate estimate to say that it would not be before 6.00 or 6.30 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that it was around 7.00 in the evening. I don't know. I'm not sure. But I know that it was already night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Anyway, in the time that you were in Grabovica, Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac arrived on one occasion only; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only time that I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And on that occasion, there was no threats or aggression shown towards the local population by Vehbija Karic. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. And when you went to this conference in Konjic that you've described, Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac themselves were also at that conference; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that they were there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your recollection, it was one of those three who distributed the tasks that were handed out at that meeting; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's how it was, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can you recall which one of them it was?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at the -- at the meeting that you've described in Konjic, you have mentioned on that occasion -- you've mentioned that a number of other commanders were there. I want to ask about the presence of -- of Sefer Halilovic at that meeting. First of all, is it your recollection that Mr. Halilovic was present at the whole meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have a clear recollection of Mr. Halilovic at that meeting? Perhaps -- well, I withdraw that question. I'll put it -- I'll put the question again. Was that meeting one which took place in a -- in a -- well, could you just describe the physical room you were in when that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a conference room of some company, some factory. I don't remember. A meeting room of some -- in some factory in the administrative building, practically in the centre of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. And to your knowledge, the 6th Corps of the Bosnian army was based in Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did they play any role -- did the 6th Corps play any role in providing transport for your troops to get to you from the tunnel down to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who provided you personally with transport to get from Grabovica to this meeting at Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Zuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it a vehicle that he put at your disposal which was on loan to you, or did he come and get you or send somebody to come and get you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he sent someone to get me then, who attended the meeting, and then later he gave me a white Yugo vehicle for my use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to ask you about that Yugo a bit later, but thank you for indicating that. But anyway, on this night, your first night in Herzegovina, you were provided with a vehicle and driver to get you to this meeting. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't use that vehicle. I was driven to that meeting by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And as regards that meeting, you went to it effectively because Adnan Solakovic hadn't yet arrived in -- in Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And you remained at that meeting, and how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Not longer than an hour or an hour and a half. Something like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. You've indicated that the tasks were handed out having already been pre-prepared before you got to the meeting. And what I want to ask you is: Did you -- was it explained to you what role Rasim Delic had to play, if any, in this particular planning and authorising of this operation?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- I don't remember Rasim Delic being mentioned, but when Mr. Halilovic was talking about the aims of the operation, he did mention that it had been approved by the Main Staff, which means that Rasim Delic must have approved it if he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did Sefer Halilovic go into any more detail than what you've just described, or did he move on to another topic?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think Mr. Halilovic spoke all the time about how important it was to carry out this operation. He didn't deal so much with who was to do what or attack along what axis. It was the commanders of the various axes who received specific orders. I did not receive any order on paper that I could hold in my hands. It was Mr. Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that was the topic I was about to get to. To the best of your recollection, the specific tasks that were given to you at the time when you were deputising for Adnan Solakovic were actually assigned to you by Zulfikar Alispago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is it the fact that -- I'm jumping forward for a moment now to another matter, and that's the relationship between your unit and Alispago's. Did your -- did you and your commander both decline to be fully placed under the command of Alispago but, rather, agreed to cooperate in the plan that he drafted?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that together we asked that we not be put under the direct command of Mr. Alispago but that the two of us should command the execution of this task together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So effectively what you did was it agree to -- to carry out the tasks that were on the plan assigned to you but not to become an organic part of Zuka unit. Is that an accurate way to put it?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And to your knowledge, that was the position taken up by the 9th Brigade or those elements of the 9th Brigade present in Herzegovina as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you went back from Konjic back to -- to Grabovica that night, I take it you got back to Grabovica pretty late at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And when you got back into Grabovica at that time, did you notice any -- anything unusual happening, any singing by soldiers or any discharging of firearms or any behaviour that was unusual?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything unusual going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you arrived back late in the night of the 8th or, if it be the case, early in the morning of the 9th, did any persons from the 2nd Independent Battalion point out to you that something funny had happened in the village, or did that happen at a later time?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't think anyone said anything to me. It was already late, and only the guards were there in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who were those guards?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Our guards in front of the house in which we were billeted. They were members of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall what the names of those guards were now?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall Zoran Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he one of the guards?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall an individual --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we go to the private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Sorry. Pardon me for that. We have to jump sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the question was: When you arrived back from the -- from the meeting, did the guards point out to you there had been any shooting or unusual behaviour of any sort during your absence?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the house in which we were billeted or, rather, in which the command was located was at the very entrance to the village, I went only as far as that house. I did not go further in and visit the soldiers billeted in other houses. I only asked the guard - and it may have been Zoran Kovacevic or someone else. I don't remember - I asked if everything was all right, and he said it was. I asked if there were any problems, and he said, no, there was just a little shooting. And that was the end of the conversation, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. So at that stage, you were told that there had been a little bit of shooting, but you weren't told anything that caused you to think that something really terrible was going on inside the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That night, nobody told me that anything so terrible had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand. And although it may not be in the military textbooks to allow this, it was the case that sometimes soldiers let off a few shots into the air just being young men, I suppose. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So that when you were told that you'd heard that there had been some shots fired, you just thought to yourself, Silly boys, and you went off to bed; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That -- yes, that could be true, because I trusted my men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And at that stage, you didn't take any measures, nor did you feel the need to take any measures, to protect the Croats and Serbs among your -- your own soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. All right. Now, I take it because you'd been travelling all of the previous night and you'd been to a meeting in Konjic, you were pretty tired and you went straight to sleep. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you had arranged a reconnaissance trip for the following morning. And we're now moving to the morning of the 9th of September. You'd arranged a reconnaissance trip. And I want to ask: You who was it that went on that reconnaissance trip with you. Was that the trip that you referred to involving Senad Pecar?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And was that also a trip that involved an individual of Albanian background called Dzeki, who was the head of a small unit called the Handzar Division?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And also -- now, I wasn't quite sure whether I'd heard you correctly about this. Was Zuka himself part of that reconnaissance, or did he just send a deputy or one of his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It was he personally that went with me to reconnoiter, Zuka Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on that occasion, is that when the white Yugo made its first appearance, or did they come in another vehicle to get you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was some kind of all-terrain vehicle that he came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What time did he arrive?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it light yet or just getting light?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It was already light. It had already dawned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Understanding that it's 11 years ago, could you do your best and try to put a time, an approximate time on when it was that you were collected by this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was around 9.00, but I'm not sure exactly. I know that it was still early, early in the morning, I mean. About 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll just work backwards from that time. Let's -- let's say 9.00. But I understand that you're not being -- you're not purporting to be exact about that. How long before that departure at 9.00 did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you wake up because of an alarm clock, or because one of the soldiers had been requested to wake you at a particular time, or did something else wake you up?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have any alarm clocks. The soldier standing guard woke me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And was that because you asked them to do that because you knew you had the job of a reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I asked him to wake me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were they the same soldiers who had been on the guard post the night before when you came home?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: There was one guard when I arrived, and there were some 20 men billeted in that house, so I can't be sure who exactly woke me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. I just really wanted to ask whether it was the same one that you met the night before or not.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's possible it was the same one, but I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did that guard, whoever it was that woke you up in the morning, have any further news to tell you in terms of shooting or unusual things that had happened in the night?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- I can't be sure about the dates now, but I think that was when they found that first dead body next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Zuka's soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want -- I'm going to ask you a number of questions about that topic because it could be a matter of importance in this case, as to when that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have a short break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will a 20-minute break, and we will resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks once again, Mr. Okovic. Mr. Okovic, before the break I was asking you questions about the reconnaissance. And when you set out on that reconnaissance, you've indicated that you went with Zuka personally. At the time when you left, Adnan Solakovic had not yet arrived in the village. That's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at the time when you set out, you didn't leave -- at that time, you didn't have any idea that there was any danger for your soldiers or anything crazy happening in the village, because otherwise you wouldn't have left. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, it was really when you arrived back late that night after the reconnaissance that you first heard of any of these really tragic events taking place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So at the time you drive out of the village to go on reconnaissance -- and we're talking now about the morning of the 9th at about -- I know you haven't been precise, but at approximately 9.00 you drove out of the village with Zuka in a jeep, and at that time you didn't see any bodies lying on the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If you had have seen bodies, you would have done something about it, I take it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. So you -- you went on reconnaissance. And can you indicate whether you were in radio contact with any persons or -- or any form of communications contact with anyone back in Grabovica during the day, or were you effectively cut off from the news while you were in the field?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: The radio connection was very bad because the communications centre hadn't yet been set up. So the connection we used for that operation was very bad, and I practically had almost no contact with my unit when I went out to do reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. When you came become late in the night of the 9th of September, can you say approximately what time - and I understand it's approximate - approximately what time you got back?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Very late at night. Very late. I think it was just before midnight or around midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I'm calling it the night of the 9th. But from what you say, it could be late on the 9th or possibly in the very early hours of the 10th; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I agree, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after 11 years, I'm not going to expect you to assign a particular date to any actions, but you may be able to recall the order of events, and so I'll ask you some questions about the order of events. You've indicated that you arrived in Grabovica on the 8th, and you've indicated that you went on reconnaissance on the 9th, and you've indicated that you arrived back in Grabovica from reconnaissance at the end of the 9th. Now, when you got back, it was at that time that you first heard that some terrible things had happened in Grabovica; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And by that time, when you came back, had your commander, Adnan Solakovic, and also Samir Pezo arrived in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. During that day when I was absent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. So you -- and it follows from that that you didn't see them arrive, nor did you observe the time at which they arrived in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. When you came back, is it accurate you were told that the old Croatian couple who had been living in the railway station with you had been rescued and taken away by a member of Zulfikar's unit, or is that something that happened later on?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember I didn't find them there, that somebody had driven them off, and somebody told me that someone from Zuka's unit or perhaps even Zuka himself -- because he had arrived just before me. He had come back. We didn't come back together from that reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we didn't arrive at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you've anticipated the question that I had. But -- and you've answered it actually, so now I don't have to ask. But so far as you know, Zuka arrived back at Grabovica just before you did, and you heard a story that he had taken the old couple away to safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Did you also hear, when you came back, that there was a concern within your unit that Croatian and Serbian members of your unit might be under some threat, or is that a concern that arose the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that during the night, we reorganised, that we knew those strange things were happening, and it was during that night or on that morning that all the members who were of other ethnic groups and who had remained - because most of the unit was already in Dreznica - that we transferred them to the command so that they would all be there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Now, I just need some details about that to the best of your memory. And, you know, please -- if you don't remember something, please tell us. But I need to ask some questions about it. Having arrived back at the end of the 9th or early on the 10th, you received the bad news about what had happened. At that time, many of your soldiers from the 2nd Independent Battalion had already left to go south to Dreznica. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Of those who were left in the village, a decision was taken by -- I'll ask you who by in a minute, but was a decision taken to pull all of your soldiers back into the house at the old railway station for their protection?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that very few people were left behind, we could all be together in that one room on the south side, and I think that practically all the men were in that one house together with the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can I just clarify that a little bit further. Did Adnan Solakovic, or indeed Samir Pezo or you, issue an instruction or an order to your men which remained in the village to come back to the old railway station and stay there with you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in the position to make decisions above the commander's head. It was the commander who decided that the men should gather in the house where the command was. All I could do was suggest it to him. I think we made the decision together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand what you say. But although you made the decision together, is it the case that Adnan Solakovic issued that order that the remaining men come back to your house?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And as far as you observed, that order was obeyed by the remaining men?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can I just ask you -- and again I know it's a long time ago, but the timing could matter. When you got back late on the 9th or early on the 10th, you've indicated this discussion took place and then you made a suggestion and Adnan Solakovic gave the order. Was that order made during the night - in other words, within an hour or two of you coming back - or was it an order given the following morning, when this -- after day broke?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when that decision was made, but on the next day all the men were in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that all the men were in the command early the following morning. Is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, although I've stayed away from ascribing dates, would you agree with me, based on what we've been through so far, that that following morning was the morning of the 10th? In other words, you arrive on the 8th in Grabovica; then on the 9th you go on reconnaissance; you get back late and get the bad news; and then early the following morning, being the 10th, the men gather in your house. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It's very possible. I don't remember the exact date, as I said. I don't know whether it was the 9th or the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand. But have I put the order of events accurately to you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Now, I want to turn to the events of the 10th. In other words, the day after you came back from reconnaissance. On that day after the soldiers were gathered in your house, you came to know of the death of a Croatian soldier from Zuka's unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And if you can help us with some details about this. Was it one of the 2nd Independent Battalion's own soldiers who brought you this news?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you subsequently speak to Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago, about the death of one of his own soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly. And I know that he was very angry because of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And when you spoke to Zulfikar Alispago about that murdered man or that killed man, was that a conversation that took place in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember where we talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me just -- I know it's a long time ago, but I just want one more question about that. Did you speak to Zuka about that on that very same day or was it on some later day?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we talked about it later, not the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Okay. Now, still remaining on this -- the day after the reconnaissance, and effectively the first day that you had bad news to deal with. Did you notice whether or not there were any new checkpoints set up in the village? Not by your soldiers but by others.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the entrance and the exit to the village, there were checkpoints set up, barriers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Did you have occasion to pass through those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you recognise the soldiers who were manning those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did they tell you whether or not they came from the 9th Brigade, soldiers who were present in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At the time when all this was happening -- can I just ask you about your reaction. I take it you were quite concerned for the -- for the safety of your own soldiers, at least the ones that remained in Grabovica, and you were concerned not to provoke any attacks on your own soldiers. Is that an accurate way to put things?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because I understand you had actually made a request in code to Vahid Karavelic to get you out of there, but you hadn't received the response that you were hoping for. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So your understanding of the situation was you had to stay in Herzegovina and you had to make the best of a very dangerous situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could understand it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, bear in mind, Mr. Okovic, that I'm a lawyer and I wasn't there. So don't let me put words into your mouth. Is that an accurate way that I've described that, or -- or not?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. The translators didn't record what you said there. I just have to ask you to answer one more time, please.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I understood your question and that you could describe the situation the way you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Very well. Now, in terms of -- of the chronology, on the 10th of -- on this day that we're now talking about, the day when all these soldiers from the 2nd Independent Battalion were drawn back to the house, on that day did you receive -- just excuse me a moment. There is an order drafted by Zuka that I want to show you and get you to have a look at. It's a combat order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown a document -- Excuse me one moment, Mr. Okovic, please. Your Honours, you've probably noticed the absence of Mr. Cengic today, and we're going to endeavour to negotiate the e-court as best we can without him. And we've been given a great deal of assistance by everyone, so now we'll try. This is Defence document -- 65 ter number D47. I think it's likely to be MFI273.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. This document's now going to be shown to you. It's a combat order headed "Defence of the people's rights, Vrdi 93." Is that on your screen yet, Mr. Okovic?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Would you mind just taking a moment to -- to inspect that document? It's a little bit lengthy. It's not necessary for you to remember every step of the planned operations and so on, but I just want you to take the chance to read over it and see -- just satisfy yourself as to what this document is before I ask you any questions about it.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: "Development of the combat assignment." But I didn't see this piece of paper. I saw a different piece of paper, handwritten. This was probably typed out later. All I saw was a handwritten order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you to confirm whether -- although this is typed, whether it says what the handwritten document said. And it might assist you to notice a couple of things. First of all, would you --

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's the same paper, but this is actually just -- it's not the original. I saw the draft material written by hand. This is an order about the attack, the axis of attack, an order for the implementation of a combat assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Okay. Would you just look --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps could the witness just be shown, please, the final page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to jump from page to page a little bit here, Mr. Okovic. I'd just like you, first of all, to have a look at the final page of that, and in particular look at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you see there that that's signed by a person -- by Zulfikar Alispago? Do you observe that?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And do you see -- do you see that the title under which he signs it is SVK PSNO commander. And does that title mean to you that he was referring to himself as a commander of a special unit of the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to what it says here, probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now we could go back, please, to the second page of this. What I'm going to ask you to look at here is just part of the order which. Concerns your unit, or purports to concern your unit anyway, and I'll ask you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English version, this is at the bottom of the first paragraph on the second page. It's the last line of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But in the Bosnian version, Mr. Okovic, you will have to find it. You'll have to help us. There's reference to an established line being held until Boraca captures the elevation of the repeater, Boraca with his right wing. And then there's a reference to soldiers of yours being brought up. And it says, "60 to 80 men," and "they have to mop up the terrain towards the cemetery." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the first paragraph or the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about -- there are two paragraphs that refer to -- let me just ask you a simple question first. Do you see a reference to Adnan Solakovic's unit there?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The units are mentioned in the first paragraph as well as the axis of activity of that unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now, looking at that -- at that document, do you recall being given those instructions by Zuka in the handwritten order that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was practically extracted from this order. Each single unit that took part in this operation, there was a yellow piece of paper specifying the axis of operation for that unit, which elevations, which points, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. So that the -- the handwritten document that was given to you only concerned your unit. Is that -- am I right about that or --

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. I understand. So you got a part of this, effectively.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I never saw this piece of paper in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. The other question I've got to ask you about is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now that document, at least in the typed version that we've got, is dated the 11th of September, 1993. Now, I understand that you're -- you're quite properly making the comment that you're not prepared to remember the exact date of things, but can I ask you, given the order of events that we've already got, your arrival on the 8th, your reconnaissance on the 9th, and now we're on the 10th, and you've gathered the soldiers back to your house and -- and so on, can you say when it was that you saw the handwritten part of this order which you've indicated you did see?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that it was the same -- on that same day, the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. All right. Now, I want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Ms. Chana?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this document is admitted into the evidence. We already have a number on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Defence Exhibit D273.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be given another opportunity to look at D270, which was the report that he wrote on the 25th of the 9th. While this documents's being -- I'm sorry. Your Honours, it's been pointed out to me that I've claimed the credit for that as a Defence document, but it's really P270.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Okovic. Now, this document might assist in continuing the chronology, which is what I'm really asking you about here. Do you have that document on the screen yet, your report?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: [Inaudible response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The interpreters indicated they did not hear your answer, Mr. Okovic. I'm sorry. Now, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Because you've got a Bosnian version, I'm just going to ask you to go to the section beginning with the words "On the 10th of September, 1993 ..." I'm going to ask you to clarify a couple of things. Do you have that paragraph in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Actually, sorry, there is one other thing I wanted to ask you about before that. Do you see that bit "On the 9th of September, 1993, was used for rest and billeting soldiers in Grabovica"? Do you see that line there?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can I just ask you this: I take it that you didn't record the facts about the bad things that really did happen in the village on that occasion for two reasons: Firstly, this is essentially a combat report and, as far as you could see, these killings had nothing to do with combat whatsoever; and secondly, because you weren't certain into whose hands this report might fall and you weren't certain whether it was safe for you to communicate that information. Have I stated that accurately?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a combat report, and it wasn't up to me to mention in a combat report something that was happening 40 kilometres behind the lines. It wasn't in my competency to do that. That is a -- that is a different question. I couldn't make the decision whether to put that in the report or not by myself. If you want to hear my opinion, though -- I was just an individual, and it would not have been wise to put that in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. That really was my question. But I take it your answer is that it wasn't up to you to decide what was in that report. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. All right. Now, returning to my original question, which concerned the 10th of September, 1993. Now, here you've mentioned that "The battalion command reached the camp of our company." Now I take it what you really meant by that was that because you were away - you had been away all day on the 9th on reconnaissance - it was on the 10th, if you like, the early hours of the 10th, that you found out about the command reaching Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. Are you thinking of the unit of the 9th Mountain Brigade or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. Pardon me. My question must have been badly phrased. No, it's just that you've written here that "On the 10th of September, the battalion reached the camp of our company." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. In reality, it appears that the battalion commander arrived the day before -- well, perhaps -- let me ask you -- I'll ask you a different question about this. Perhaps I'm -- I'm going down the wrong path altogether. Where do you get these dates that you've put in this report? Did you get the dates from other notes that you'd taken?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I have that from my notes. I kept notes of what I did each day in relation to the combat assignment. So we only have fragments in this report. We didn't really go into detail of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's -- I wondered about that. Okay. Well, look, could you go on to the next section, then, that commences -- that concerns the 11th of September? Do you have that part? It's the next paragraph, I think.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's still on page 1 of the B/C/S version but on page 2 of the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So on the 11th of September, we can conclude that there was a further command reconnaissance of the Vrdi region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And later -- look at the end of that paragraph, if you wouldn't mind. Later on, you had a meeting - and this is later on on the 11th - you had a meeting with the commander of the Zulfikar detachment. When I say "you," I mean Solakovic had a meeting with the commander of the Zulfikar detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And then on the 12th, the unit or parts of your -- of your company went down to a place near to Arapovo Hill; is that correct? And while you're looking at that, when you get to the point where you need to turn over the page, you say so and the court staff will help.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then on the 13th of September, your units concluded some further reconnaissance in the area of the repeater, the repeater station?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And then on the 14th of September, your unit arrived at -- or near to Dreznica and commenced participation in some combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In particular, the occupation of the road from Vilina Polja.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And later that day, the HVO resistance was noticed and further plans were made for the use of your units in combat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And on the 15th of September, further combat took place in which your units or parts of them were engaged. And then later in the day Zuka, Zulfikar Alispago, ordered that some of your units were allowed to rest from combat for a while; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. And just indicate when you need the page to be turned over, because I'm working with an English version here. Then on the 16th of September, because you met a great deal of HVO resistance, an attack was then directed towards the hill known as Medvjed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I've got some questions about the fighting at Medvjed partly because other witnesses are going to be called who were following and listening to this fighting on a radio. So the fighting at Medvjed was led by Zulfikar Alispago, who was present - not actually running up the hill of Medvjed, but nearby - leading the action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And during the time of that -- the attacks on Medvjed, those attacks seemed at the time to be progressing very successfully, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 17th, the whole of your unit, with the assistance of some soldiers of the 9th Brigade and the Zulfikar detachment, continued the advance and reached the targets that you were supposed to reach; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, a hill called Golubic was occupied and captured; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then on the 18th of September, your unit was again involved in fighting and once again fought alongside parts of the Zulfikar detachment and the 9th Motorised Brigade in the area of Medvjed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you in the position -- sorry, and perhaps I should ask you this: During that fighting, which soldiers appeared to you to be leading the 9th Brigade men? In other words, who were the senior 9th Brigade people leading their soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't have direct communication. I just heard it over the radio, and I was only paying attention to what was happening to our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I take it it was a pretty hot fight.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. On the 19th of September, did Zulfikar Alispago issue an order to fortify the lines which you had successfully reached and to withdraw some combat units?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in particular did Zulfikar Alispago on the 19th of September, 1993 withdraw from combat units of the 2nd Independent Battalion, the 10th Brigade, and the 9th Brigade, and that order was complied with on the evening of the 20th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but it was the other way round: The 9th and the 10th were pulled out first, and we were the last to be pulled out of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, can I just ask you about that. Were they pulled out on the same day as you but earlier in the day, or were they pulled out a day earlier than you?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea about the time, but they were pulled out before us, before our unit, because we had some casualties, some killed and wounded, and we should have pulled out earlier. This -- the terrain was quite rough. We had to use mountain-climbing equipment and ropes in order to bring out the dead and the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, could I ask you this: By the time you came out, the units of the 10th and the 9th had already gone; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any members of the 9th or the 10th in Grabovica, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you -- when you were pulled out, you and your units went back to Grabovica briefly; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you've indicated when you passed through Grabovica you saw no soldiers from the 9th or the 10th on that occasion. Now, my question is: Were you asked --

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I was the last to arrive in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Were you asked by Zulfikar Alispago or indeed by Sefer Halilovic to remain in Herzegovina to help hold the lines and to hang onto what had been gained?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: My commander told me they were saying we should stay and that he was opposed to us staying. We were supposed to keep those positions. However, he said we had done our job and that we should now go back to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Who was it who -- according to what Solakovic told you, was it Halilovic who asked him to stay in Herzegovina or Zuka?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I know the answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, could I ask you this question, then: Do you know whether or not Adnan Solakovic was in contact with Zuka at around that time?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I was the last to arrive in the village when our last soldier had withdrawn from the combat positions, I don't know what had been going on either in the command or in Grabovica. I don't know who he had contacted. But both he and I insisted that we withdraw to Sarajevo. Who it was who asked him to say, that we should stay, well, I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's okay. Whoever it was who asked, was not obeyed. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a question about communications equipment and the -- and the setting up of a base. You indicated to me -- I'm going back now to early in your arrival at Grabovica. You indicated that you went out on reconnaissance the day after you arrived and that you were gone most of the day. You'll recall I asked you some questions about communications equipment and you said it was pretty bad. Can I ask you this question: Once Adnan Solakovic arrived down in Herzegovina, do you remember whether or not that old railway station became something of a communications base? In other words, was any radio equipment installed there after Adnan came?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We installed our own radio equipment there. The equipment arrived with the commander, and we set up our communications there that we used internally for our own use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And was it using that -- sorry, just to be clear, was that -- when -- let me just start that again. I'm sorry. The question ran away from me. When you came back from your reconnaissance trip on the second day and you saw Adnan, Samir Pezo, and you heard the bad news, was the communications equipment already set up at that point, or is that something that you did the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: We struggled to set up this connection with Sarajevo throughout the day. It was a big problem to set up this equipment, the antennas and so on, and we waited for a long time to send this message to Sarajevo, because we were unable to establish the communications. The equipment wasn't functioning properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And it was on that equipment that you ultimately sent the coded message which was shown to you by the Prosecutor early on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Are you able to say now whether that -- Just excuse me a moment. I just want to check a date. Would you excuse me, Mr. Okovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What I'm searching for here, Mr. Okovic, there's no secrets about it. We have a copy of that coded message that you sent, and it's got a date on it, and I just want to be able to put the date to you accurately.

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So if you'd just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll -- sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Okovic, the date on that document was the 11th of November -- oh, sorry, pardon me, the 11th of September. And my question to you is this: When you -- when you set up that radio equipment, you've indicated it took a long time for it to become functional and it took you a long time before you could send that message. Is it possible that the message did not get sent until the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZAKIR OKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I think it was on that day in the afternoon that the message was sent and that our communications officer struggled the whole day to get the equipment working. We would probably have sent it much earlier than we did had the equipment been functioning properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I understand your answer. And then just to preserve that chronology, it was later on that day -- or that evening -- sorry, I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've got a new topic to go to now. I think there's probably another half hour of cross-examination altogether remaining for this witness. It might be appropriate to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we could break here. Well, Witness, I believe I have to keep you here for another day. As I did say to other witnesses, do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I wish you have a good rest today, and we will resume tomorrow afternoon. And by the way, I would like to say that on Thursday afternoon, we are still sitting in this courtroom in the afternoon, not in the morning. I hope nobody made any plans yet. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, although it is an entirely private matter, may I -- we are sitting in the morning on Fridays -- on Friday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's a plan which might, if it's now changed, result in the death of counsel at the hands of his family but we will act upon it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for this. But anyway, the hearing for today is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
